data.title: The Nor'easter
data.rumour: Big storm coming. Get your batteries.
about: A whodunnit in a storm. Hal sells you his granddad's brass hurricane lamp to pay for plywood before a nor'easter (§{halLamp}). Mrs. Ochoa comes looking for anything that makes light and offers $70 for it (§{stormBuyer}).

When the storm hits (§{noreaster}) the power goes on Water Street and Hal, Mrs. Ochoa and young Jory shelter in your shop. Around midnight your best piece is swapped for a fake (or, if there's nothing worth taking, the till is $20 short). Question them: each remembers a clue about who brushed past in the dark (fish and oilskin, a ball of wool, a phone screen). With the lamp you can ask two; without it your phone dies after one. Name the right one and the real thing comes out from under a coat (Caught in the Dark); guess wrong or wait till morning and you're left with the fake (Lights On).

hurricaneLamp.name: Brass hurricane lamp
tells: A ship's hurricane lamp, brass and glass, with a full reservoir of oil. It works.

halLamp.title: Hal sells his granddad's hurricane lamp before the storm

text: Hal Mayhew. Big storm coming. A proper nor'easter, the radio says. Get your batteries.
Thing is, I need cash for plywood more than I need this. My granddad's hurricane lamp. It'll light a room when the power goes, and it will go.

steps.text: It'll hit {placed:noreaster} night. Half of Water Street loses power every time. If your lights stay on, expect company.

stormBuyer.title: Mrs. Ochoa wants anything that makes light

steps.text: Do you have batteries? Torches? Candles? A lamp? Anything that makes light? Every shop on the street is cleaned out.

then.text: Then I'm going to be very bored in the dark.

then.why: Sold the hurricane lamp before the storm

choose.label: "That one's not for sale. I'll need it."

noreaster.title: The nor'easter: a power cut, and a swap in the dark

narrate.then: The nor'easter hits after dark. At nine the power goes on the whole of Water Street, and you light the hurricane lamp. Within the hour three neighbors are in your shop, dripping.
narrate.else: The nor'easter hits after dark. At nine the power goes on the whole of Water Street. By the light of one phone, three neighbors shelter in your shop, dripping.

steps.note: best: the best thing on the shelves, which gets swapped; culprit: 0 Hal, 1 Mrs. Ochoa, 2 Jory, at random

narrate.then: Somewhere around midnight, in the dark between gusts, you hear the shelf creak. The {best.name|lower} is still there. But it doesn't look quite right.
narrate.else: Somewhere around midnight, in the dark between gusts, you hear the till drawer slide. Twenty dollars short.

text.then: Me? I was by the door holding it shut.

else.then: Somebody brushed past me in the dark. They smelled of fish and wet oilskin.
Somebody brushed past me in the dark. They had a ball of wool in their pocket. I felt it.
else.else: Somebody brushed past me in the dark. They had a phone screen on, just for a second.

steps.note: story moment (witness): Hal is warm or a friend, wasn't the one, and tells you what he saw

text.then: Between us: it was Mrs. Ochoa at your shelf. Saw it plain when the lightning went. I wouldn't say it for anyone else.
text.else: Between us: it was Jory at your shelf. Saw it plain when the lightning went. I wouldn't say it for anyone else.

then.text: ...Fine. FINE. It's under my coat. I was going to give it back. Probably.

then.narrate: The real thing comes out from under a wet coat. The fake goes in the bin. The storm blows itself out by four, and everybody pretends to be asleep until it's light.

else.text: Me?! I've been sat here the whole time!

else.narrate: The power comes back at dawn. By then your three neighbors have gone home, and in the daylight you can see it plainly.

clues.text: A copy. Somebody swapped it in the storm.

epilogue.line: Water Street still talks about the night of the nor'easter, and who had what under their coat.
You never found out who swapped the fake onto your shelf. You have a list.
